/*
 * Makes everything awesome if you are Andrew.  Some day it will make everything
 *  awesome if you are not awesome too.
 *
 * Right now the most meaningful thing to know is that if XPCOM failures happen
 *  (and get reported to the error console), this will induce a unit test
 *  failure.  You should think this is awesome no matter whether you are Andrew
 *  or not.
 */

source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: Current _init_log_helper documentation still describes network endpoint detection and conditional xpcshell wrapping, while its inspected body creates console instances and initializes the tunnel. The file introduction also promises unit-test failure from console XPCOM errors, but the inspected observer dumps messages and catches errors. Proposed local documentation check: state the actions this helper performs and identify any external failure policy separately. This is a comment-to-source discrepancy, not proof that the whole test harness never fails on console errors. This is static source and test-code inspection. No runtime, build, lint or live accessibility check ran. Full Bugzilla and historical review timeline and inline discussion remain pending; source landing does not prove approval of a proposed manual rule.
title: Update logging comments to match the current behavior they describe
